object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. evidence.span: Uniform preprocessing makes it straightforward to compare modalities within the same technology. Figure 2 shows a comparison of data from three different DOGMA-seq (Mimitou et al. 2021) modalities as assayed in (Z. Xu et al. 2022), all preprocessed with cellatlas and the tools it uses: snATAK, kallisto bustools, and kITE. Uniform preprocessing also allows for quantifying the efficiency of assaying the different modalities. The fact that the RNA and protein libraries have a similar number of UMIs captured for a given number of reads (Figure 2a,b) is consistent with similar dilutions of the libraries (1.99nM and 2.2nM respectively), whereas the tag library efficiency (Figure 2c) is distinctly different, likely as a result of dilution to 0.27nM.
